## Claimed + dispatched — `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat

PM session `session_01CSoz9uGhaaSgiq3hshtN7L`, branch `claude/issue-6034-confirm-runtime-close-parity`.
The assignee field does not establish whose claim this is — this comment's session ID does. No earlier claim comment exists.

### 裁决 (binding)

The two confirm runtimes **agree on open** (pinned by #5835's parity test) and **diverge on close**: `useConsoleActionRuntime` blanks the whole state; the sibling preserves fields.

**Converge the close handlers on one reset shape, and extend the existing parity pin to the close path.**

⚠️ **Extend the existing pin — do not write a second one.** #5835's parity test already owns this relationship; a new parallel test would leave two pins that can disagree, which is the same class of defect as the two runtimes.

⛔ **If a close-path consumer genuinely depends on the divergent shape, that is a finding to REPORT — not a reason to keep both.** Report it and stop on that half; do not preserve the divergence behind a flag.

### PM机制假设 (verify)

1. Both runtimes still diverge on close as described, and #5835's parity pin still covers **open only**. Re-derive on today's `main`.
2. **Which reset shape is correct** is your call to make from the code — the card does not rule it. Blanking and field-preserving are observably different on a reopen; establish which one consumers actually rely on before picking, and say why in the PR body.
3. Enumerate the close-path consumers of both runtimes. ⚠️ A convergence that lands on one runtime's callers and not the other's is the "fix three of four sites" trap that bit two cards tonight — #6111's card named six sites when the key was dropped at **two hops**, and #6110's named four when there were **six**, one of which would have shipped the whole fix inert.

### Traps

⚠️ **Parity pins can pass by degenerating.** If your fixture's confirm state is empty or single-field, "blanked" and "preserved" look identical and the pin proves nothing. **Use a multi-field confirm state**, assert the specific surviving/cleared fields by name, and prove the close-path assertion **red before the fix** on whichever runtime you change.

⚠️ **The open-path assertions will stay green either way** — they are #5835's and are controls here, not evidence. Say so in the PR body.

⚠️ `pnpm --filter <pkg> exec vitest` / `cd packages/x && pnpm exec vitest` hit a guard (objectui#3378) — one form **refuses loudly** (`ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_FIRST_FAIL`), another **silently runs `apps/console`'s 22 files and reports them green**. **Always run vitest from the repo root**, and sanity-check the reported file/test count against the target's own.

⚠️ `tsc` resolves workspace deps through **`dist`** while `vitest` aliases to **`src/`** — a type-check red can be unbuilt siblings, a real error, or both (a dev tonight got 15 errors: 14 noise + 1 real). Build the closure, then classify each remaining error by name.

### Standing rules

Predict direction before running; prove mutations on disk by grepping injected AND separately removed text; print the landing site; assert anchor uniqueness; restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with a **cwd-independent** command and confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` empty. Derive gates by enumerating **each CI job's own step list**. Cached turbo green is not a measurement — `--force`. Commit before you ablate. Changeset: a behaviour change on close — state it in words; ⛔ never `major`.

### Collision bounds

`packages/app-shell` is a large shared package and **two other agents have touched it tonight** — ⚠️ **#6165** is live in `packages/app-shell/src/console/home/` (`HomeRail.tsx`, `HomePage.tsx` + tests), and #6224's PR #6265 deletes `packages/app-shell/src/utils/metadataConverters.ts` (draft, not yet landed). **Different files is fine; same file is not.** Check before editing and ⛔ **report any file-level overlap rather than resolving it yourself.**

Seven other agents are live elsewhere — ⛔ do not edit `packages/plugin-form/**`, `packages/components/**`, `packages/plugin-list/**`, `packages/plugin-detail/**`, `packages/types/**`, `packages/core/**`, `packages/plugin-kanban/**`, `packages/plugin-map/**`, `examples/schema-catalog/**`, `apps/site/**`.

⛔ Leave the PR **draft** — the PM lands it.

### ⚠️ Note for the next dispatch

This card was the reason **`packages/app-shell` was treated as occupied** all morning, and three other workstreams were bounded away from it on that basis. That constraint is now lifted — but ⚠️ `app-shell` still carries **open draft [PR #6283](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/pull/6283)** on `views/metadata-admin/previews/block-types.ts`. Different area, but check before editing.

## Re-claimed + dispatched — `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat

PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`, branch `claude/issue-6034-confirm-runtime-close-parity`.
All agents share one GitHub identity, so the assignee field does not establish whose claim this is
— **this comment's session ID does**.

Prior claim history read in full: the 05:56Z claim belongs to `session_01CSoz9uGhaaSgiq3hshtN7L`,
whose agent died, and `os-litant` correctly reclaimed the card to `pm:queue` at 09:16Z. Both of
those sessions are gone. No live claim stands, so this is a clean re-dispatch, not a takeover.

### ⭐ The 05:56Z dispatch order is carried forward intact — I am not rewriting it

That order is sound and specific, and its author being gone does not make its ruling wrong. It
stands as written, in particular:

- **Converge the close handlers on one reset shape, and extend #5835's existing parity pin to the
  close path.** ⚠️ **Extend the existing pin — do not write a second one.** A parallel test would
  leave two pins that can disagree, which is the same defect class as the two runtimes.
- ⛔ **If a close-path consumer genuinely depends on the divergent shape, that is a finding to
  REPORT — not a reason to keep both.** Do not preserve the divergence behind a flag.
- **Which reset shape is correct is the dev's call from the code**; the card does not rule it.
  Establish which behaviour consumers rely on before picking, and say why in the PR body.
- ⚠️ **Parity pins can pass by degenerating.** With an empty or single-field confirm state,
  "blanked" and "preserved" are indistinguishable and the pin proves nothing. Use a **multi-field**
  state, assert surviving/cleared fields **by name**, and prove the close-path assertion **red
  before the fix**.
- ⚠️ **The open-path assertions stay green either way** — they are #5835's and are **controls**
  here, not evidence. Say so in the PR body.

### Pre-dispatch gate, re-run on `origin/main` `9602dc820`

- **(a) Whole thread read** — 3 records, all above.
- **(b) Shadow check, in-flight *and* batch.** Both target files are in `packages/app-shell`.
  Nothing in flight touches it: #6154 (`packages/types/src/field-types.ts` + `packages/fields`),
  #6271 (`plugin-kanban`), #6353 (`plugin-timeline`), #6373 (`plugin-dashboard` +
  `packages/types/src/data-display.ts`), #6375 (`data-objectstack`, delivered). #6412, which held
  an app-shell surface under another session's claim, has **merged**. Surface is clear.
- **(c) Call-site census** — the divergence reproduces exactly as the card describes, and it is
  two lines:

  | | open | close |
  |---|---|---|
  | `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` | `:193` `setConfirmState({ open: true, message, options, resolve })` | `:696` `setConfirmState({ open: false, message: '' })` — **blanks** |
  | `RecordDetailView.tsx` | `:518` — identical shape | `:2511` `setConfirmState(s => ({ ...s, open: false }))` — **preserves** |

  Open paths agree; close paths differ. The pin to extend is
  `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.confirmRuntimeParity-5835.test.tsx`.

⚠️ The earlier order warned about the "fix three of four sites" trap. My census finds **two**
`setConfirmState` reset sites and no others in `packages/*/src`, but that count is mine on today's
tree — ⛔ re-derive it rather than inheriting it, and if you find a third consumer at a second hop,
that is the trap firing and it changes the card.

Deliver a **draft** PR with `Fixes #6034`. ⛔ Do not mark ready, ⛔ do not self-merge, ⛔ do not
enable auto-merge — the PM lands it.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**

PR #6432, head `1dd499571`. `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session
`session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`. Verified on a pinned ref (`refs/pmtmp/6034`).

One line of production change: `{ open: false, message: '' }` → `s => ({ ...s, open: false })`.

### ⭐ The reset shape was decided from the consumer chain, and that turned a tidy-up into a real defect

The dispatch left "which shape is correct" to the dev and asked it to establish what consumers
rely on. It traced the chain end to end: `confirmState` appears on exactly four lines in
`packages/*/src` (two `useState`, two dialog mounts), and the only reader is
`ActionConfirmDialog` — which **keeps reading `state.message` and `state.options` through Radix's
exit animation.**

Corroborated on `origin/main`: the shipped dialog carries
`duration-200 … data-[state=closed]:animate-out`, so Presence holds it mounted ~200ms after close.

⭐ **Blanking therefore rewrote the dialog's visible text mid-fade** — description emptied, title
and both button labels reverted to their i18n defaults, in front of the user. That is a
user-visible defect, not a consistency nit, and it was found by following the consumer rather than
by picking the prettier shape.

The retained `resolve` is shown inert rather than assumed so: the dialog settles the promise
**before** it asks for the close, and the open path replaces the whole state object, so nothing
stale survives a reopen.

### The "fix three of four sites" trap was checked, not assumed

Five mount sites (`ConsoleShell.tsx:83`, `ObjectView.tsx:1060`, `DeclaredActionsBar.tsx:463`,
`PageView` via `ConsoleActionRuntimeProvider`, plus `RecordDetailView`'s own) — but **each runtime
owns its reset in exactly one place**, so the one-line change converges four at once and the fifth
was already the target. No third consumer at a second hop.

⭐ And it checked the one way a hop hides: `plugin-designer`'s name-colliding `ConfirmDialogState`
(`isOpen`/`title`/`message`, 7 consumers) — *"checked because a name collision is exactly how a
third hop hides."* Not a hop, correctly not filed.

### The pin was extended, not duplicated

`RecordDetailView.confirmRuntimeParity-5835.test.tsx`: +139 lines, **second `describe` block in
the same file**, two blocks total. That was the explicit instruction — a parallel pin would have
left two guards able to disagree, the same defect class as the two runtimes.

Red-before-fix, prediction stated first: 6 pass / 2 fail expected, **exactly that observed**, with
the diff naming the divergence itself — `expected [ 'message', 'open' ] to deeply equal
[ 'message', 'open', 'options', …(1) ]`. Green after: 8/8. Ablation re-run post-commit, mutation
proven on disk by grepping injected *and* removed text plus a blob-hash change, restore verified
against the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty.

⭐ *"First ablation attempt was a genuine null result — the EXIT trap restored the file before the
test ran; re-run with the measurement inside the same script."* Reporting a botched measurement
instead of quietly re-running it is what makes the rest of the numbers worth reading.

### Out of scope

**#6431** — `ActionParamDialog` carries the same close divergence between the same two runtimes.
Correctly not folded in: `ParamDialogState` carries `params` and in-flight collection state, so
blanking on close **may be deliberate there** rather than the mid-fade defect. ⭐ And the negative
result is what bounds it: `ActionResultDialog` does **not** diverge (both close with
`{ open: false }`, which is also its initial state), so the drift is two dialogs of three, not
three of three. A negative result recorded is what stops the next card being scoped by assumption.

⚠️ One discipline note: #6431 was filed carrying **`domain:ui`**. `domain:*` is the triage seat's
single-producer output — a dev (or this seat) applying it pre-empts that. Harmless here since the
routing is obviously right, and ⛔ I am not removing it, because churning a label to make a point
is worse than the breach. Recorded for the dispatch template.

### Landing

⛔ Not enqueued — 20 green, **8 still running**, 0 failures, `behind` (⛔ not syncing; it resolves
unaided here). It goes to the queue when they land.
